findings.issue: The wholesale-claim contract between A31 and A32 still contradicts itself; the check-1 fix moved ownership one way in A31 while A32 was moved the other way. A31 (sections 0, 3, 5) says A32 calls in-process issueClaim, revokeClaim and replaceClaim inside its own transactions, owns the 05:00 expiry sweep and the 60/30-day reminders, and that A31's sweep never touches topic 3 and emits no claim.expiring. A32 (sections 'A31 owns the on-chain claim' and 'Claim agreement with A31') says A32 never calls A31 synchronously, publishes classification.valid, renewed and revoked on the outbox, and relies on A31's 02:00 sweep to emit claim.expiring (at 60 and 30 days) and claim.expired, which fire SM-02 valid->expiring and expiring->expired. The enums disagree as well. A32 imports 'A31's frozen set' {certificate, s708_500k_offer, sophisticated_s761GA, professional} and asserts equality in a test; A31 defines {accountant_certificate, ticket_500k, sophisticated_s761GA, professional_s9}. A32's claim_state has no pending_identity or off_chain_only. Concrete failure: when a certificate reaches its expiry, no node fires SM-02 expiring->expired and no node removes the WHOLESALE_AU claim; the 60/30-day reminders never fire; A32's cross-node enum test fails. A31's own forged-event challenge (a classification.valid inserted in the outbox) also assumes the outbox model that its section 3 rejects.
findings.fix: Choose one contract and write it identically in both notes before Specify. Because A32 depends on A31, record it in A31 and make the A32 row in section 0 list every A32 text that must change, not 'accept the executor interface unchanged'. Recommended: keep the in-process executors and move the reminders and SM-02 timers to A32, which A31's text already assumes; state that A31 publishes claim.issued, claim.revoked and claim.expired on the outbox for A32's claim_state; and have A32 drop its reliance on A31's sweep and on claim.expiring. Put the basis enum in one place (A03 packages/domain, or A31's topics.ts), choosing one spelling set, and add off_chain_only and pending_identity to A32's claim_state. Reword the forged-event challenge to match the chosen transport. Escalate if A32's owner does not accept.

findings.issue: The topic model contradicts A24's frozen spec. A24 makes WHOLESALE_AU an acquisition topic, enforced by its AcquisitionClaimModule, and keeps it out of the identity registry's required topics: holding topics are 1, 2 and 4. A24's tests assert that a lapsed or revoked WHOLESALE_AU leaves isVerified TRUE and makes a mint or a cross-identity transfer fail on AcquisitionClaim, and forced transfers do not run moduleCheck. A31 says instead that the wholesale pack 'requires 1, 2, 3 and 4', proposes a new WholesaleEligibilityModule that 'drops topic 3 from required topics', and its challenges assert (a) 'isVerified must already be false for new receipts' when the wholesale claim expires and (b) 'forcedTransfer must revert on chain on a token that requires topic 3'. Under A24 both assertions fail on a correct build, so Fable either fails a correct build or the builder bends the contracts. A24 also defines topic ids as keccak256 constants; A31 hard-codes 1 to 5 in topics.ts, the IdentityClaim.topic column and the removal-request 'topic in {1, 2, 4}', and says a test fails if they differ from ClaimTopics.sol.
findings.fix: Rewrite section 3 and the Money/holdings and Ticket-scope challenges against A24's model. At expiry, isVerified stays true, a mint or a cross-identity transfer reverts on AcquisitionClaim, and a sale or a move to the holder's own wallet passes. Replace 'forcedTransfer reverts on a token that requires topic 3' with 'forcedTransfer is refused off chain by A28's destination guard (G04 through A19); on chain it is not blocked (a documented limit)'. Restate the A24 follow-up as an extension of AcquisitionClaimModule, a per-offer ticket list checked as an alternative to the topic-3 claim, not as a new module. Use A24's keccak topic constants, keyed by name, everywhere.

findings.issue: The ONCHAINID key layout and the recovery path contradict A24. A24's frozen layout is createIdentityWithManagementKeys(wallet, salt, [R]), after which the recovery key R adds V4 as a CLAIM key and the wallet as a MANAGEMENT key; A24 tests that 'V4 cannot add or remove a management key', and A31 is meant to call A24's helper createInvestorIdentity. A31 instead makes V4 the temporary management key, has V4 add the wallet and remove itself, and says the smart wallet ends as the sole management key, with no R. A24's recovery sequence also needs A31 to registerIdentity(new) with the country copied from the lost wallet, and later to deleteIdentity(lost) once the balance is zero. A31's section 1 allows deleteIdentity only under the 'Revoke on-chain eligibility' 4E, classification.revoke or confirm_match, and its reason codes have no recovery. Concrete failure: either A15's allow-list refuses V4's addKey or removeKey on a correct A24 build, or J09 recovery needs a second, unrelated 4E approval by the MLRO or CCO, which breaks the rule that one approval ID binds admin and custody.
findings.fix: Adopt A24's layout: A31 calls A24's createInvestorIdentity, V4 is a claim key only, and R's holder is named (A29 or A28). Remove addKey and removeKey from V4's allow-list request. Add to the section 1 table a row 'registerIdentity(new) and deleteIdentity(lost) bound to A28's recovery or forced-transfer approval_id', with the precondition balanceOf(lost) == 0 on every token and a reason code 'wallet_recovery'. Add a J09 challenge that runs A24's two-trust recovery sequence end to end under one approval ID.

findings.issue: The meaning of the identity registry's country is wrong against A24 and A30. A24's frozen spec says country is the G06 classification code: 36 when A30 classifies the account as not a foreign person (Australian citizens wherever they live, permanent residents, Australian-controlled entities), otherwise the nationality code or the controlling jurisdiction. A24 flags that A31 'must write the G06 classification code instead'. A31 still writes 'ISO 3166-1 numeric of the confirmed residency (AU = 36)', and its residency challenge uses 'from AU (36) to a country'. Concrete failure: an Australian citizen living in London is registered with 826 and refused by CountryAllowModule; a temporary-visa holder living in Sydney is registered with 36 and accepted on an established-residential trust, a FIRB/G06 breach.
findings.fix: In section 2 and section 4, derive country from A30's foreign_person classification exactly as A24 item 2 defines it (36 when not a foreign person, else the nationality or controlling-jurisdiction code). Add A24's vectors (citizen abroad gives 36 and is accepted; temporary resident gives 554 and is refused on a residential trust) to the G06 challenge and the oracle scope.

findings.issue: The registry_status contract with A29 is circular and contradictory. A29 (frozen) says registry_status uses 'A31's vocabulary exactly' {unregistered, registering, registered, stale, deregistered}, that A31 writes it only through setRegistryStatus(walletId, status, {txHash, event}) with unregistered->registering->registered, and that the ONB-08 labels are A31's: 'Linked', 'Pending identity review', 'Not yet linked'. A31 says it writes no Wallet row and only publishes identity.registered for A29 to apply. It also uses statuses A29 does not have (eligible, deleted), conditions registration on registry_status in {unregistered, eligible}, and cites labels 'as A29 defines them' with different text ('Ready to link', 'Pending identity verification'). Concrete failure: A29's contract test rejects eligible and deleted; nothing ever sets registering; neither node owns the label strings; the Design fidelity challenge asserts 'Pending identity verification', which A29 and A56 do not produce.
findings.fix: Own the vocabulary and the labels in A31, since A29 defers to it: define the five statuses, the three labels, and the mapping from the case state to 'Pending identity review'. State that A31 calls A29's setRegistryStatus (registering on submit, registered on the confirmed IdentityRegistered, deregistered on deletion) instead of an outbox apply. Remove eligible and deleted. Align the Design fidelity challenge strings.

findings.issue: The A30 interface is still mismatched. (1) A30 ships GET /v1/internal/kyc/accounts?state=approved&unregistered=true, which returns INV- account ids, not /kyc/cases. (2) A30 emits kyb.entity.owners_pending and kyb.entity.owners_verified, expects A31 to suspend and restore the entity's eligibility claim, and A30's G03 challenge requires 'an on-chain transfer through A31's claim must be refused at once'. A31 neither consumes these events nor models the case, and its section 1 condition treats refresh_due (the state an owners_pending entity sits in) as verified. (3) kyc_valid_until and restriction are per person, but A31 applies them to the 'investor' (an account that can be joint or an entity) without defining how members combine. (4) A30 emits investor.residency.changed on a KYB recompute or an owner change without any 4E approval, but A31's updateCountry requires a 4E approval_id. Concrete failure: an SMSF adds an unverified owner and stays isVerified on chain, so it can receive tokens; A31's poll hits a route that does not exist; an entity's foreign-person flip is never written on chain.
findings.fix: Use A30's account query and ids. Consume owners_pending by removing KYC_VERIFIED (an AUTO binding on the hash of A30's entity status, or a declared binding A15 accepts) and owners_verified by re-issuing it. Add a challenge that mirrors A30's G03 case. Define the account-level condition: kyc_valid_until is the minimum across member persons, and the account counts as restricted if any member is restricted. Add a section 1 binding for residency changes that come from A30's KYB recompute (an AUTO hash of A30's foreign_person record), or ask A30 to route every flip through the 4E.

findings.issue: A31 ignores the on-chain identity providers that A15 and A28 expect from it, and it lacks a dependency. A15 says the on-chain check behind IdentityRegistryReader (the P4 destination guard) is 'added by A31'. A28 says A31 registers the on-chain check behind its IdentityLookup port and re-runs A28's tokenops/ports/*.contract.test.ts at A31's gate. A31 mentions neither. A28 is not a dependency of A31, yet A31's Ticket-scope challenge and its section 0 follow-up rely on A28's destination guard, forcedTransfer path and per-offer ticket list. Concrete failure: P4 and TOP_DESTINATION_UNREGISTERED stay off-chain only, and nobody proves the promised on-chain check; the orchestrator can schedule A31 before A28 has passed, so the ticket challenge cannot run.
findings.fix: Add A28 to A31's deps in app-graph.json and in the Depends-on line; there is no cycle, because A28 depends on A15, A18, A20, A27 and A29. Add to section 3 an exported on-chain provider (IR contains plus isVerified at the latest block) registered for A15's IdentityRegistryReader and A28's IdentityLookup. Add a pass criterion that A28's port contract tests and A15's provider conformance cases pass against it.

findings.issue: Some challenges and pass items rely on nodes or codes that do not exist at A31's gate. (1) 'Anomaly events at A101': A101 is neither an ancestor nor a dependent of A31, so it may not be built. (2) The snapshot challenge expects A20's R5 to report 'untrusted_issuer', but A20's R5 finding type is only claim_drift. (3) A42 is expected to call restampSanctionsClear, but A42 has no edge to A31 and A42's spec never mentions the call, so A42 can build first and never call it, and every SANCTIONS_CLEAR claim lapses after 30 days.
findings.fix: Emit the internal-route refusal as an audit event plus an A12 or A13 anomaly signal that A101 consumes later, and assert that event. Change 'untrusted_issuer' to A20's claim_drift, with the issuer named in the finding detail. Add A31 to A42's deps (no cycle) and list the A42 call as a required follow-up, or run the restamp from A31's own worker job reading A42's latest result through a stubbed port.

findings.issue: The node header and the graph data are stale against the spec. The Depends-on line omits A29 and says A29 'must be added' to app-graph.json, but the graph already lists it. Unlocks omits A49, which the graph lists. The graph summary still says 'only for KYCCase rows in state approved', 'wholesale claim with a two-year expiry', 'R4/R5 checks feeding recon', 'revoke as 4E; residency change as 4E', and its oracle line reads 'isVerified true only after an approved case'. All of these contradict the spec, which now covers per-function conditions, validity copied from A32, a snapshot only, and executing A30's approval. An oracle writer or the orchestrator working from the node data would test the old behaviour.
findings.fix: Add A29 (and A28, per the finding above) to the Depends-on line and delete the 'graph follow-up' paragraph. Add A49 to Unlocks. Rewrite the app-graph.json summary for A31 to match the spec's first paragraph and oracle rule.

findings.issue: The 6-10 agent-hour estimate is low for the scope: a V4 op builder with per-function conditions and a source reader, about 18 audit events, 3 worker jobs plus consumers, 4 end-to-end chain fixtures, 5,000 fast-check sequences, a 1,000-step audit run, 100% branch coverage and several cross-node contract fixes. The comparable A30 was raised to 12-18.
findings.fix: Raise the estimate to about 10-16 agent-hours in both the note and app-graph.json, or split off the snapshot and sweep jobs.
